title: Fuzz finding triage
description: Triage of the findings in one fuzz run record (V2-18). Every finding has exactly one entry: either the failure is already caught by an existing cell, detector and fixture, or it is new and those three artifacts now exist, or it is not a bug with a stated reason. The record is checked by tools/fuzz_triage.py against the fuzz run itself; it is not proof that the routing decision was right, only that the named artifacts exist.

record.description: Path of the fuzz run record these entries triage.

cells.description: Path of the cell registry the cell and detector fields resolve against, relative to --root. Required by tools/fuzz_triage.py when any entry names a cell; an empty triage file for a clean record does not need it.

entries.description: One entry per finding in the record. An empty list is valid only for a record with no findings.

input_sha256.description: Hash of the failing input, as recorded in findings[].input_sha256.

disposition.description: covered: an existing cell, detector and fixture already catch this failure class. new: no detector caught it, and the cell, detector and fixture now exist. not-a-bug: the input violates a documented contract, so the finding is the contract working.

cell.description: Cell that owns the failure class. Required unless disposition is not-a-bug.

detector.description: Detector that catches the failure. It must belong to `cell` in the registry passed with --cells. Required unless disposition is not-a-bug.

fixture.description: Mutation fixture that demonstrates the failure, in the `path#MUT-ID` form used by the cell registry. Required unless disposition is not-a-bug.

reason.description: Why the input is not a bug. Required for disposition not-a-bug; the reason is the whole point of the entry.

note.description: Free-form context: the observed output, the fix, or the follow-up.
